sentences.text: A taxonomic re-evaluation restricted the genus Anaerovibrio to the single species Anaerovibrio lipolyticus, placing two other former species in the new genera Anaerosinus and Anaeroarcus.
Anaerovibrio lipolyticus is a rumen bacterium that has been recognised as one of the major species involved in lipid hydrolysis in ruminant animals.
A study of its draft genome identified three putative lipase genes, and the expressed enzymes showed higher hydrolytic activity against caprylate, laurate and myristate.
In pigs, a study reported Anaerovibrio among taxa with significantly higher relative abundance in mucosa than in digesta of the cecum and ileum.
A field study of piglets reported that Anaerovibrio was among the groups that increased after weaning in animals with postweaning diarrhea.
